Internship Test and Interview Experience
Reshmika Nambiar
reshmikasnambiar@gmail.com
rsnambiar_b19@ce.vjti.ac.in
TY B. Tech Computer Engineering
2019-2023 Batch
SAP Labs
Internship Test
DATE : 05.09.2021
It was a test of 45 mins, conducted on the SHL Platform, at 10 AM. There were only 2
very simple coding questions:
1.
There was a shop and some customer IDs were given. Customer IDs which were
perfect squares had some special discount. Basically, we had to print the number
of perfect squares in the given array.
2.
There was a row of 8 houses (I think?) which were represented by 8 cells. They
could be either active (1) or inactive (0). For each day, if the neighbouring cells
were both the same, the resultant cell would be 0, else 1. This had to be done for
a given number of days and the resultant array had to be printed.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/active-inactive-cells-k-days/
You could switch between questions. And there were many options for languages. You
could use several header files and the whole program had to be written, not just one
function.
I wrote very simple programs for both without thinking too much about optimization.
These were very simple questions and I completed and submitted the test in 15-20 mins.
I was quite surprised because in the previous SAP Internship Tests, there used to be
many more questions with higher difficulty, plus MCQs as well.
16 selected candidates for the next round were announced on 7th, noon. Some of those
candidates were already selected for other companies before the SAP Labs interview, so
they were removed from the list and new candidates to replace them were announced
on the 7th at midnight.

Internship Interview
16 Candidates
DATE : 08.09.2021
Technical Interview 1 — 16 Candidates
My interview took place at 10:45 AM. Different time slots were provided for different
candidates. It took place on MS Teams.
I was not asked to introduce myself here, but prepared raho with a short intro.
The interviewer first said that he had gone through my resume and GitHub profile and
asked me which project I had worked the hardest/spent most time on. Then he asked me
to explain that project. After my explanation was done, he did not ask any further
questions and moved on to the core topics.
These are the questions that I remember:
For OS, he asked :
What is thrashing?
What are some page scheduling algorithms?
For CN, he asked :
What happens when you type a URL in the address bar? (Here, I said we had just
started CN, so I wasn’t very clear about it. But I still answered it.)
In the case of a WiFi router, which topology is used? I replied with tree topology and he
then asked why it can’t be a bus topology.
For all the CN questions, I gave an approximate answer which he seemed okay with for
the most part.
For DSA, he asked :
What is a circular linked list?
Can the next pointer of the last node of a circular linked list point to some node other
than the first node (means, to some node in the middle)?
What is a doubly linked list?
What are its advantages?
What other data structure do you know that can be traversed in both forward and
backward directions?
Some more general questions he asked :
What is polymorphism?
Coding Questions :

He shared with me a Codeshare.io link where both of us could type code. It had syntax
highlighting and language could be selected/changed at any time. But the code couldn’t
be run.
He asked me to implement runtime polymorphism using code.
Then, he asked me to reverse an array, but in place (without using any extra array).
He also asked me to write a code to detect a loop in a linked list.
The interview was almost 45 mins long. He finally asked me if I had any questions for
him.
Technical Interview 2 — 8 Candidates
Different time slots were provided for different candidates. It took place on MS Teams
like before. My interview was scheduled for 12:30 PM, but got postponed and actually
took place at 1:30 PM. By that time the rest of the candidates had already finished with
their round 2 interviews and 6 of them had been selected for the next round. This made
me a little confused, but the interviewer simply told me that they will take my round 3
interview if this one goes well.
The interviewer first introduced himself and then asked me to introduce myself. I thought
he would ask questions about my projects, but for some reason, I wasn’t asked any (but
others were, so I guess it depends on the interviewer).
Some of the questions I remember were:
He asked how I would rate myself in SQL (out of 10). Then he gave me a table,
Employee, which he typed in the MS Teams chat as follows-
empid     empname      mgrid
12            Ajay
23
23
Rohan
56
56            Rahul
-
Obviously the values were not the same, but it was something like this.
He asked me to write an SQL query to select the employee names and their manager’s
names. (This had to be sent through the MS Teams chat, which was quite inconvenient).
Then he asked a question and I had to write the code for it and send it via chat.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/trapping-rain-water/
The question was similar to this. Basically, an array of numbers of blocks at each
position was given and the total amount of water which it could hold had to be printed. A
pseudocode could be written for this, but I wrote C++ code itself.

Then he asked me two simple puzzles.
1.
If I had a box of 50 green socks and 50 blue socks, what is the minimum number
of socks required to make a pair if I pick socks from the box one-by-one
randomly? (https://datagenetics.com/blog/march42018/index.html)
2.
You have 25 horses. You can make 5 horses run in a race at a time. What is the
minimum number of races required to find out the top 3 horses (with rank)?
(https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-9-find-the-fastest-3-horses/)
Would you get an error/what would be the output if you did this? -
int[] ab = new int[30];
int[] cd = new int[50];
ab = cd;
The interview went on for almost an hour. He finally asked me if I had any questions for
him.
HR Interview — 7 Candidates
After the second round, I was called for the third round and a slot was allotted to me after
all the other candidates finished their R3 (round 3) interviews. So, around 4 PM.
This was only for 10 mins, again on MS Teams. The ma’am was very polite. She asked
me if I was tired after all these interviews. She then introduced herself, and then asked
me for my introduction. She asked me about my family and where I was from. She asked
me which SAP Labs location(s) I would prefer and if I would be okay with other locations
if I don’t get selected at my preferred ones. She told me that usually we would be
assigned the Bangalore one. She finally asked me if I had any questions for her.
Finally, 6 people were selected for the internship, including me. This was announced at
around 5:15 PM.
General Tips
1. Don’t be nervous. It’s okay if you don’t know everything. They are mostly just
looking for the way you approach problems. So even if you are not able to
completely solve a question, it is okay.
2.
Ask the interviewers for clarifications regarding questions. They give a lot of hints
to help you solve the problems.
3.
Always ask the interviewer something when they ask you whether you have any
questions for them. Be prepared with some questions beforehand.

4.
You can say that you are not sure about some answer before answering in case
you haven’t studied some topic.
5.
Also, if you already know some coding question/puzzle which gets asked, you
can say that you have seen it before. They want to see your approach. If you
already know something, then it is hard to pretend like you don’t and then arrive
at the answer (at least, for someone who is bad at lying like me :P ). This
obviously doesn’t apply to everyone. Kar sakte ho tho kar lo.
6.
Sometimes lagta hai ki round bahut kharaab gaya, next round k liye nahi honge
select. But be ready because aisa zaroori nahi hai. They can select you and
announce it late. Unless they explicitly tell you that you are out, stay alert and
keep checking WhatsApp/mails for new messages.
7.
Before and during the interview, keep checking your emails and messages. For
some companies, extra candidates were announced on the day of the interview,
in the morning. Jaldi utho just in case, at least for the interview days.
8.
Aisa mat socho ki you haven’t prepared anything tho nahi hoga. I only prepared
for 1 week before the internship test. (In my case, I had only applied for SAP
Labs, and not the other companies. But others had applied for the companies
which came before SAP Labs as well.) Seniors k experiences dekho and
common questions practice karlo achhe se, especially ones previously asked by
the company/ies you are applying to. Geeksforgeeks se practice karo questions.
https://practice.geeksforgeeks.org/explore/
Go through company archives.
9.
Thoda tiring hota hai having all the interviews on the same day. And the timings
are also announced erratically. Wake up early and have breakfast, and interviews
k beech mein lunch/snacks khaa lena. Eat light but eat something which will give
you enough energy. Try sleeping early before the interview.
Finally, ALL THE BEST! :)
Ho jaega, tension mat lo
